rows.label: Lead per tonne of whole lead-acid battery
rows.basis: Basel guidelines (2003, table 16): an SLI battery is 17% metallic lead and 50% lead salts and oxides, about 51–60% lead depending on the paste. Frost & Sullivan (2025): 60–70% of battery weight. India's EPR certificate example uses 65%. The catalogue converts at 0.6.
rows.source: Basel Convention technical guidelines, 2003; Ardee Industries DRHP, p. 145; EPR certificate mechanism (TNPCB copy)

rows.label: Lead per tonne of lead waste and scrap (HS 7802)
rows.basis: Assumption. No published average found; the code mixes battery plates, cable sheathing and soft lead.

rows.label: Lead recovered per tonne of lead fed to a smelter
rows.basis: 0.90 is the conversion factor that India's EPR certificate mechanism applies to recovered metal; 0.95 and 1.00 (no loss) are assumptions. Smelter intake = lead output ÷ recovery.

rows.label: Years from sale to scrapping
rows.basis: Basel guidelines (2003, §2.5): car batteries last 6 to 48 months, up to six years in ideal conditions, and only 30% reach 48 months. India's EPR mechanism sets the target for automotive lead-acid batteries sold in 2019–20 in 2022–23, three years on. Ghana: battery imports averaged over years t−4 to t−2; India: consumption in year t−3.
rows.source: Basel Convention technical guidelines, 2003; EPR certificate mechanism (TNPCB copy)

rows.label: Spent lead-acid batteries exported, 2023
rows.basis: UNCTAD's estimated weight, with its range: all went to India, which recorded 1,047 t from Ethiopia. Ethiopia reported 4,023 t at about USD 99 a tonne, a weight UNCTAD treats as implausible for the value. Replaces the trade figure in Ethiopia's balance.
rows.source: UNCTAD Global Battery Trade Monitor (UN Comtrade; UNCTAD calculations)

rows.label: Refined lead consumption, 2021
rows.basis: Hindustan Zinc reports that India's refined lead consumption rose 9.4% to 1.2 Mt in 2022, so 2021 ≈ 1.2 Mt ÷ 1.094. High case: the 2022 figure itself (a two-year battery life).

rows.label: Share of lead consumption that goes into batteries
rows.basis: Frost & Sullivan: over 80% of the lead consumed in India is used in battery manufacturing (Ardee DRHP, p. 142). 0.85 and 0.90 are assumptions above that floor.
rows.source: Ardee Industries DRHP (F&S report, Sept 2025), p. 142

rows.label: Recycled lead production, FY2024–25
rows.basis: Frost & Sullivan: about 1.26 million tonnes (Ardee DRHP, p. 144).
rows.source: Ardee Industries DRHP (F&S report, Sept 2025), p. 144

rows.label: Registered recyclers' share of recycled lead
rows.basis: Central: Frost & Sullivan market shares of recycled lead ingots in FY2024–25: six named groups 45.0%, Bindal 0.5% and about 660 other CPCB-registered recyclers 15.6% (61.1% together), unorganised 24.4%, imports 14.4%. Registered share of domestic supply = 61.1 ÷ (61.1 + 24.4). Low: Autocar Pro (4 Aug 2026) puts the informal share at about 40%, citing no source.
rows.source: Ardee Industries DRHP (F&S report, Sept 2025), pp. 150–151; Autocar Pro, 4 Aug 2026

rows.label: Battery waste recycled through registered recyclers, Aug 2022–Dec 2025
rows.basis: Ministry of Environment reply in the Rajya Sabha, Dec 2025: around 58.26 lakh tonnes of battery waste recycled since the Battery Waste Management Rules were notified in Aug 2022, all battery types. Over 40 months that is about 1.75 Mt a year; used as the high case for registered intake.
rows.source: MoEFCC written reply, Rajya Sabha, Dec 2025 (reported by EQ Mag, 19 Dec 2025)

rows.label: Months covered by the EPR figure
Lead scrap generated in India each year (cross-check)
rows.basis: Frost & Sullivan: about 750,000–850,000 t a year, 85–90% of it from used lead-acid batteries (Ardee DRHP, p. 145). Not used in the calculation; compare with lead in India's own used batteries.
rows.source: Ardee Industries DRHP (F&S report, Sept 2025), p. 145

rows.label: Unorganised share of recycled lead ingot market, FY2024–25 (cross-check)
rows.basis: Frost & Sullivan market shares (Ardee DRHP, pp. 150–151): 24.4% unorganised, by value, of a market that includes 14.4% imports. Not used in the calculation.
rows.source: Ardee Industries DRHP (F&S report, Sept 2025), pp. 150–151

rows.label: Used lead-acid batteries generated a year
rows.basis: Wilson's 2021 inventory for Pure Earth: 402,903 t a year from about 925,000 t of batteries in use (vehicle and battery counts from around 2020), with car and motorcycle batteries lasting two years, commercial three and solar five. Low: the same stock with three-year car and motorcycle batteries and four-year commercial ones. Lead content uses the lead fraction above.
rows.source: Wilson ULAB inventory, Indonesia (ILA for Pure Earth, Mar 2021; copy on file)

rows.label: Secondary lead produced by industrial smelters, a year
rows.basis: Central: USGS's estimate of secondary refined lead for 2022. Low: refined lead exported in 2024 (UN Comtrade), a floor, since Indonesia's battery makers also use recycled lead. High: the formal licensed sector's capacity in Wilson's 2021 inventory (106,000 t of lead bullion), run full. Smelter feed = output ÷ recovery.
rows.source: USGS Minerals Yearbook 2022 (via IndexMundi); UN Comtrade; Wilson ULAB inventory, Indonesia (Mar 2021)
